clue.text: Spring rain returns, initially deepening the Don perhaps

parts.note: a spring of mineral water is a spa

indicators.note: returns means the word rain is read backwards
initially picks out the opening letter of deepening

explanation.surface: Spring showers come back and gradually make the Don river deeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RAIN into NIAR. The Don looks like the Russian river, but a don is a Spanish gentleman, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Don is the title of a Spanish gentleman, so a don is an example of a native of Spain.

clue.text: Thinly spread butter and jam?

explanation.surface: Toast spread sparingly with butter and jam.
explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions pose as breakfast spreads: to spread butter thinly is to scrape it, and a jam is a fix or predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape butter is to spread it very sparingly; a scrape is also a tight spot or predicament.

clue.text: A female fairy upset when I leave the encounter

indicators.note: upset tells us to jumble the remaining letters into a new order
when I leave says the letter I departs from the word fairy

explanation.surface: A fairy, a girl, is cross when someone walks out of the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I leave' takes I from FAIRY to give FARY, and 'upset' rearranges that into FRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight or brawl, a violent encounter between people.

clue.text: Coves silent it turns out

indicators.note: it turns out suggests the word silent emerges in a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Some bays prove to be quiet places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it turns out' rearranges the letters of SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Coves and inlets are both small sheltered bays along a coastline.

clue.text: Colourful boss intent, we hear

parts.note: intent spoken sounds like 'in tent': the flamboyant person in charge under the big top of a circus

explanation.surface: A vivid manager is reportedly very determined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intent' reads as determined, but heard aloud it is 'in tent', placing the colourful boss under a circus big top.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-coated figure who presents the acts in a circus is its flamboyant boss inside the big top.

clue.text: Organised detectives off?

parts.note: to organise or manage something is to run it, past tense ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: Have well-run detectives gone rotten?
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department. 'off' looks like a direction but means gone bad, like milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is spoiled and smells rotten.

clue.text: Bond's flirtation, having lost head?

indicators.note: having lost head means the first letter of the flirtation word is dropped

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual flirtation or brief affair

explanation.surface: James Bond's romance seems to have lost its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes James Bond and his flings, but 'Bond' is just the definition and DALLIANCE loses its head D.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond between parties, such as a treaty or union, is a formal pact.

clue.text: His pieces are not necessarily soothing

definitions.text: His pieces are not necessarily soothing

parts.words: His pieces are not necessarily soothing
parts.note: a calming person composes others, but this writer of music produces works that may be loud or harsh

explanation.surface: A man whose work isn't always calming.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for someone who calms things down is identical to the word for a writer of music, whose pieces may be anything but calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music produces pieces, and nothing says those works must be gentle or calming.

clue.text: Preparing mayonnaise, say?

explanation.surface: Making a salad sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing a chicken or a wound is preparing it; mayonnaise is an example of a salad dressing, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress food is to get it ready for cooking; a sauce poured on salad, like mayonnaise, is also called by this name.

clue.text: The few have a go creating a lottery

parts.note: The Few were the RAF pilots of the Battle of Britain, named in Churchill's speech
to have a fling at something is to have a try at it

explanation.surface: A small group try their luck by setting up a prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The few' is Churchill's name for the Royal Air Force (RAF) pilots who fought the Battle of Britain in 1940.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a raffle means organising a draw where tickets win prizes, a type of lottery.

clue.text: Served thus, brandy is opened and put into fire

indicators.note: put into says the letter goes inside the fire word

parts.note: a flame is fire

indicators.note: is opened points to the opening letter of the word brandy

explanation.surface: A dish arrives after brandy is uncorked and set alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is opened' gives the first letter, B, of brandy, which 'put into' places inside FLAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Food served flambé has spirit poured over it and set alight at table.

clue.text: Happy period when class distinction is less obvious?

definitions.text: Happy period when class distinction is less obvious?

parts.words: Happy period when class distinction is less obvious?
parts.note: class means a school class rather than social rank: at break pupils of every form mingle in the yard

explanation.surface: A golden age when social hierarchy fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class distinction' suggests social rank, but it is school classes, which mix in the playground at break.
explanation.definitionFit: The school break is a cheerful interval when pupils of all forms play together outside.

clue.text: Note — farmhouse victim is renowned

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
in the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so the victim is a mouse missing its last letter

explanation.surface: A note says the person killed at the farmhouse is well known.
explanation.walkthrough: The farmhouse victim is a mouse from the nursery rhyme Three Blind Mice, where the farmer's wife cuts off their tails, so MOUSE loses its tail E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone renowned is widely known and celebrated.

clue.text: A travelling-case!

parts.note: case is a medical patient, and this one travels to hospital for treatment rather than staying in a ward

explanation.surface: A suitcase for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling-case' looks like luggage, but a case is a patient, and this one comes in for treatment and goes home the same day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital case who visits for treatment without staying overnight travels to and from the clinic.

clue.text: From hence, scout fashions a key-hole plate

indicators.note: fashions means shapes the letters of hence and scout into something new

explanation.surface: Starting from here, a Boy Scout makes a metal cover for a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashions' rearranges the ten letters of HENCE and SCOUT; 'From' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a heraldic shield, this word names the ornamental plate around a keyhole.

clue.text: High control of delights on credit

parts.note: joys are delights
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Pleasures bought on credit get out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit. 'High control' is the lever a pilot uses high in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's control column is operated aloft, making it the pilot's steering lever up in the sky.

clue.text: Guys curse their clothes?

parts.note: guys are men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Blokes swear at the outfits they wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' refers back to the guys, so the definition reads as men's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing made for males is sold in a gents' department under this name.

clue.text: Teatime's changed for judge

indicators.note: changed signals rearranging the letters of teatime's into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Teatime has been moved to suit a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges TEATIMES, the S here counting as a letter. 'judge' is a verb, not the magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity is to gauge or reckon it roughly.

clue.text: Takes longer rest as bowling drops off?

parts.note: an over is a spell of six balls bowled in cricket
drops off means falls asleep, sleeps

explanation.surface: A cricketer dozes too long while the bowling continues.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sleeps beyond the intended waking time stays in bed resting too long.

clue.text: First signs of interference generally upsets a North African lizard

indicators.note: First signs of takes the opening letters of interference, generally and upsets

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for African

explanation.surface: Meddling usually unsettles a lizard from northern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' looks like an anagram signal but is only fodder for the first letters; 'North African' splits into N and A.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tropical American reptile is a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Corked and stamped

explanation.surface: A bottle stoppered and a letter franked.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle that is corked is closed tight; a document stamped with wax or a seal has been authenticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Corked means closed tight, as a bottle is; stamped means marked with an official impression.

clue.text: A wild horse on the beach

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of horse running out of order

explanation.surface: An untamed horse runs along the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges HORSE into SHORE after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land rather than at sea, beside the water, means being on the shore.

clue.text: Eurasian finch is coming back to hide!

indicators.note: coming back means the word is runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A small bird returns to conceal itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns IS into SI; 'hide' looks like a verb but is a noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This small yellow-green songbird of Europe and Asia belongs to the finch family.

clue.text: Is amazing, to old hands wearing a G-string

indicators.note: wearing says the old hands have something on them, wrapped around it

parts.note: old stagers are veterans, old hands
the letter G is the string named by G-string

explanation.surface: Veteran showmen in skimpy costumes astonish an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hands' are STAGERS (as in 'old stagers'), who are 'wearing' the G from G-string inside them. 'Is amazing' is a verb phrase, 'staggers' as in astounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that staggers you astonishes you so much you nearly reel.

clue.text: Chilling character in O'Neill' play?

parts.note: refers to the title figure of Eugene O'Neill's drama about a salesman whose name suggests frozen water and cold

explanation.surface: A frightening role in a play by Eugene O'Neill.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill's play is The Iceman Cometh; 'Chilling' suggests frightening, but the character literally deals in ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of O'Neill's play is a man who delivers frozen blocks, literally a chilling figure.

clue.text: Its eastern dishes cannot be taken out!

definitions.text: Its eastern dishes cannot be taken out!

parts.words: Its eastern dishes cannot be taken out!
parts.note: dishes means attractive women, kept in a secluded oriental household and never escorted on dates, not food unavailable as takeaway

explanation.surface: An oriental restaurant that does no takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishes' and 'taken out' suggest a restaurant without takeaway; really they are attractive women in a sultan's harem, never taken out on dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem, the secluded women's quarters of a Muslim palace, houses wives who are kept confined.

clue.text: Officer said to be a bit of a nut

indicators.note: said to be signals that the officer's rank is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a colonel is an army officer

explanation.surface: An army officer is supposedly a little bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: COLONEL is pronounced like KERNEL. 'a bit of a nut' suggests mildly mad but means part of a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible inner part of a nut is its softer seed core.

clue.text: Bestride the street and mark with red

parts.note: to raddle is to mark with red ochre, as on sheep

explanation.surface: Stand over the road and paint it red.
explanation.walkthrough: Raddle is red ochre that farmers use to mark sheep; to raddle is to mark with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to sit or stand with one leg on each side of it.
